prerequisites: Basic command of the basic subjects of the degrees

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing and material properties.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude in work and willingness to learn, considering the need for continuous training that the exercise of the profession will undoubtedly demand.
Apply the strategies of scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively; propose hypotheses and solutions using the models typical of Engineering.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions in the development of tasks typical of technological subjects.
Properly use the specific terminology of the subject, expressing the basic fundamentals of Materials Science through the correct use of verbal, mathematical and graphical language.
Distinguish the main types of materials and relate their different characteristics to their diverse applications.

Link the internal structure of materials with their specific physical-chemical and mechanical properties, establishing the impact that these properties have on the practical function of each material.
Manage the concept of a material's equilibrium state and reason how a mechanical or thermal treatment can change this state and, therefore, the material's properties.
Work cooperatively on tasks framed within the scope of Materials Science, tackling team tasks and analyzing and discussing ideas contributed by other team members.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Structure of condensed matter. Crystalline and amorphous structure. Material groups. Crystalline lattice defects. Diffusion phenomena.
Topic 2. Solidification. Solidification mechanisms. Phase diagrams.
Topic 3. Material manufacturing. Obtaining and transformation of metallic, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials. Natural resources, synthesis, recycling.
Topic 4. Material properties. Mechanical, electrical, and magnetic properties of materials and their relationship with structure. Material testing. Other physical and chemical properties.
Topic 5. Modification of material structure. Thermal, thermochemical, and thermomechanical treatments. Effect on material properties.
Topic 6. Engineering materials. Metallic, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials. Properties, classification, and applications. New materials for new applications.
Topic 7. Service conditions and failure diagnosis. Corrosion, fatigue, creep, wear, and aging conditions. Failure analysis.
Topic 8. Material selection. Criteria for material selection: service requirements and economic criteria.
LABORATORY PRACTICES: Heat treatment (Quenching and tempering of metal specimens)
LABORATORY PRACTICES: Mechanical tests (Charpy, tensile, hardness)
LABORATORY PRACTICES: Metallography (sample preparation and observation)
LABORATORY PRACTICES: Electrical and magnetic properties of materials
teaching_methods: Lectures with student participation in occasional debates
Autonomous learning activities (ABP, cases) (potentially for small groups)
Consultation and following instructions on eGela
Work on sustainability-related issues (IKD-i3 model, ODS)
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, all evaluation tests must be passed. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required for each assessed component: written exam, theoretical content tests (average of three tests), and laboratory practical deliverables. The final grade is an arithmetic average considering the specified weights. In the extraordinary call, scores of approved theoretical tests and lab deliverables from the ordinary call are retained. Students re-take only the failed components, or if all components were failed or it's a first-time submission, they will take two written exams (theoretical 70%, practical 30%), each requiring a minimum score of 5 out of 10.
